THE PANIC CONJUNCT IS THE ONE AN ORDINARY BATTERY DOES NOT REACH. A slot leaked by a panicking worker ratchets the in-flight ceiling down over the process's life until the listener admits nothing — a local denial of service that no error path reports, reached by whatever input made the worker panic.

A PATH GUESSED ONTO A ROUTE sends a request to an audience it does not name, and the audience is what the signature binds; a default route reached by a path that names none would do that silently. The host and content-type guards keep a browser or a non-loopback peer from driving the operator's signing identity.

A PAUSE RENDERED AS A FINISHED CALL reports a call that has NOT run as one that has — the same class of error the execution contract exists for, at the last hop before the local client acts.

THE CLOSE AND THE CONTENT-LENGTH are how a refusal reaches the caller as an unexplained broken pipe instead of the refusal it was given: closing on top of unread bytes turns a 405 into an RST, and the refusal path may therefore WAIT, bounded in both bytes and wall clock, while the success path may not — what a reset discards there is a VERIFIED reply to a call the server already ran.

WHAT HAPPENS TO AN ADMITTED REQUEST, NOT WHOSE ARE ADMITTED: the bind scope, the accepted authority and the head fields are client.local_ingress_authority's under THM-0091. No number is asserted sufficient.
